measurements.title: Wrist path deviation
measurements.description: How far does your hand wander from a straight path during the punch?
measurements.figure_text: The red trail follows your wrist. The dashed line shows a straight path from start to finish. The circle appears when your wrist reaches its largest deviation.
measurements.graph_text: See how the distance changes during your punch. Drag along the graph or tap Show maximum.
measurements.method_text:
We draw a straight line from your wrist’s starting position to its finishing position. Maximum deviation is the greatest distance from that line.

Typical deviation (RMS) summarizes the distances across the punch, giving larger deviations more weight.

A smaller number means a straighter path in this camera view. It does not, on its own, mean a better punch.

measurements.title: Wrist speed
measurements.description: How fast does your hand move during the punch?
measurements.figure_text: The red trail follows your wrist. The circle appears when your wrist reaches its fastest point.
measurements.graph_text: See how your speed changes during the punch. Drag along the graph or tap Show maximum speed.
measurements.method_text:
We calculate speed from how far your wrist moves and how long it takes.

To keep small tracking wobbles from making the graph jumpy, we look at several nearby frames together. In this example, that covers about 0.05 seconds before and after each moment. Near the start and finish, we use the available frames.

This smooths the speed curve. It does not change the movement shown in the animation. A very brief burst of speed may look slightly lower or wider, and its highest point may shift a little.

Maximum speed is the highest point on the curve.
